fieldNotes.operationalStatus: OPERATIONAL. This is a BLANK-FLAG entry on the BlueTriton facility list, but it is NOT a closed/demolished site. It is the historic Arrowhead / Nestle Waters / now Primo Brands Los Angeles bottling plant at 1566 E Washington Blvd, Los Angeles CA 90021 - one of the oldest continuously operating manufacturing facilities in LA (state-of-the-art plant opened 1917 at Washington Blvd & Compton Ave; bottled Arrowhead 100+ years). Oct-2025 Street View shows an active site: a 'PRIMO' building sign, the '1566' office building, white process water tanks/silos, an American flag, a live health-grade 'A' placard by the entrance, and an active ReadyRefresh delivery-fleet yard full of box trucks plus stacked palletized bottled-water product. The 2024 USFS shutdown order only affected the Strawberry Creek / San Bernardino spring pipeline source, NOT this LA bottling/distribution plant, which uses LADWP municipal water plus trucked spring water. Operational verdict: ACTIVE.
fieldNotes.siteResolution: No coords were supplied. Web research (PBS SoCal 'Lost LA', BBB/D&B business profiles) placed the plant at Washington Blvd & Compton Ave; the Primo/BlueTriton corporate address of record is 1566 E Washington Blvd, LA 90021. Google geocoding of that address returned 34.0205477,-118.2449874, which lands dead-center on the bottling complex. Confirmed by Street View showing the '1566' building number and 'PRIMO' signage at this exact spot.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE. Oct-2025 Street View (pano EpKRc0zekfxg0iXXea__xw) at the Washington Blvd frontage shows a wide black sliding security gate across the truck/yard driveway, set in a fenced perimeter wall (barbed wire on top), beside the 1566 office. Clear controlled entrance.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE. No staffed booth (1-3 vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) at the gate. The entrance is controlled by the sliding gate plus a blue directional/check-in sign panel mounted at the gate - no guard structure.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: TRUE. There is a controlled truck gate but no guard shack -> implies kiosk / call-box / app or buzzer check-in. The mounted signage panel at the gate is consistent with self/remote check-in.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban. Dense downtown-LA industrial fabric (ZIP 90021), wedged between the rail corridor / I-10 approach to the N and residential blocks to the S/W; surrounded on all sides by warehouses and city streets.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: TRUE. The gate opens directly onto E Washington Blvd, a busy arterial, with very little apron/stacking room before the public sidewalk; an inbound truck queue would spill straight onto the street. Tight urban geometry.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: TRUE (drivewayLong FALSE). The gate-to-yard approach is short - the gate is right at the street and the internal yard begins immediately behind it; only 1-2 trucks can stage in the approach before reaching the dense interior yard.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: TRUE. A large paved internal yard inside the gate (between the buildings) serves as the holding/queue/maneuvering area before docks; product pallets and delivery trucks stage there.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Banded 10-25. The internal building faces fronting the central paved yard carry a bank of loading/dock doors (the south face of the main warehouse building shows a regular rhythm of bays). Exact count is hard from overhead because the dense urban roofs and the internal-courtyard orientation hide some faces; honest estimate ~14, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Banded 10-25. Multiple over-the-road trailers parked without tractors along the south/west perimeter and interior rows, plus a large block of stacked palletized product. ~18 trailers/vans visible.
fieldNotes.dropYard: TRUE. The southern/western portion of the complex is a dedicated trailer + delivery-fleet storage lot (rows of box trucks/vans and parked trailers), distinct from the active dock staging.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: TRUE. The property is a campus of several connected/adjacent large buildings (bottling plant building with process tanks, the 1566 office building, a warehouse/load building, and a separate west building over the fleet lot) on one fenced block.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Cannot confirm separate ship vs receive dock clusters from overhead in this dense interior-courtyard layout; defaulted FALSE, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE. A rail corridor runs along the north side of Washington Blvd, but no spur enters the Primo property; trucking only.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 4 - bottling plant w/ tanks, 1566 office, central warehouse/load building, and a west building over the delivery-fleet lot, all on one contiguous fenced parcel.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~8 acres derived from the perimeter polygon (~212m N-S x ~157m E-W block, complex fills most of it).
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Mixed delivery-fleet + trailer use; practical capacity ~40 across the yard rows and west fleet lot. Approximate.
fieldNotes.imageryQuality: Maxar/Airbus 2026 satellite is sharp; Oct-2025 Street View confirms operations and the gate. High confidence on operational status, gate, urban setting, dropYard, campus. Dock count is the main soft number due to the interior-courtyard orientation.
